packets.title: Preserve local Telegram cancellation and unspecified flood-wait diagnostics
packets.scope: Implement only the root-approved Telegram CLI cancellation and unspecified flood-wait diagnostic correction in P048-P072-WORKER-HANDOFF.md. Preserve local prompt cancellation across adapter wrapping without forwarding arbitrary errors; keep existing credential, cooldown and source-enrollment behavior.
acceptance: Preserve local prompt cancellation using fixed safe wording and the existing cancellation/usage classification, including when a provider adapter wraps the prompt exception.
Keep duration-specific guidance for a positive safe retry_after; retain the wait class without inventing a duration when it is absent or unusable.
Leave provider error sanitization, connector authentication, cooldown persistence, retries, app credentials and source enrollment architecture unchanged.
Retain generic fallback for unknown exceptions; do not forward all Error/ConnectionError/provider messages.

At phone, code and password prompts, ordinary local cancellation produces the fixed cancellation diagnostic and UsageError classification consumed by existing CLI dispatch; no success output or new connection is recorded and normal cleanup runs.

Map a classified flood_wait with retry_after=120 to duration-specific wait wording; map the same code without a usable duration to wait-specific wording with no fabricated count or immediate connectivity retry advice.
An ordinary unreachable error still uses the existing generic connectivity diagnostic.
Existing unknown prompt-error sanitization, missing app credentials, successful enrollment and cooldown tests retain their assertions.
Request the assigned focused tests through root's qualified runner; preserve all failures, source ownership and existing assertions.
limits: Only the three assigned relative write paths. No connector source/core/auth/credential/provider/account/controller/service/native changes.
No vulnerability, timing or resource reproductions; use ordinary synthetic error and enrollment cases only.

packets.title: Report a fixed pre-capture Claude health warning on initial and repeat import
packets.scope: Implement only the frozen root P072 warning contract in P048-P072-WORKER-HANDOFF.md: a fresh pre-capture Claude health observation emits a fixed bounded stderr warning when degraded, labeled as health check before capture and partial/unsupported content. Apply initial/repeat imports; preserve blocked-health behavior, stdout counts and exit semantics. Never render arbitrary health.detail or claim capture-exact diagnostics.
acceptance: For initial and repeated Claude imports, perform a fresh health observation before capture and emit a fixed bounded stderr line only for degraded health, clearly labeled as a health check before capture and partial/unsupported content.
Never print arbitrary health.detail, file/export path or message content, and never describe the observation as the exact captured snapshot.
Keep existing initial blocked-health and source-consent behavior, tolerant partial-import success, stdout counts and process exit semantics.
A clean ordinary two-message export imports normally with no new warning; unchanged repeat stores zero new events.
An ordinary export with supported text plus an unsupported content part retains supported content and emits the same fixed warning on initial and repeated import, with existing counts/exits.
Request the new public lifecycle test through root's qualified runner; preserve assertions and failures. P071's accepted attribution tests remain untouched.
limits: Only import.ts and the new assigned lifecycle test. No parser/snapshot/shared-helper/core-ingest/doctor/status/count/schema/P071-test/docs/controller changes.
No real/private export files or account/service/native operations.
No vulnerability, timing or resource reproductions; use ordinary synthetic exports only.
